chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who advanced oil to a man upon the condition that he would take butter from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on advancing oil with the condition of repaying in butter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'Gharar' (uncertainty) and 'Riba' in pre-Islamic and early Islamic trade practices, specifically regarding the exchange of different foodstuffs with a delay. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares the transaction invalid because it involves swapping one type of consumable good for another with a deferred repayment, which can lead to exploitation or ambiguity in quality and quantity. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise specification and immediate equivalence in spot trades to avoid usurious elements.
